 ❯ explain the cache plan for project-a

 ● The cache in project-a needs a clear eviction policy. If every entry lives forever, memory pressure grows until the process is stopped by the limits of its lane. A
   bounded LRU keeps hot entries near the front while cold ones fall off the back, and it costs one map and one list per instance.

   Start by measuring hit rates under the current workload. Add counters to src/lib/cache.ts and run test/app.test.ts to establish a baseline. Once the baseline is stable,
   introduce the capacity limit and assert that evictions happen when the threshold is crossed, and not before it.

   The final design should keep reads fast, avoid lock contention across lanes, and store the new counters alongside the existing metrics so the dashboard can display them
   without an extra query. None of this changes the public interface that the rest of project-a calls.

   1. Add the LRU map to src/lib/cache.ts and expose get, set and delete methods that match the existing interface, so that no caller has to change; keep the capacity a
      constructor argument with a sensible default, and document why the default was chosen next to it.
   2. Write a test in test/app.test.ts that fills the cache beyond its capacity and asserts that the oldest unreferenced entry is removed first.
   3. Document the eviction policy in a comment so future readers know why the limit exists.

   - Keep the public API unchanged.
   - Avoid adding dependencies: the standard library already has everything the cache needs, and every new dependency is one more thing to audit, pin and upgrade across
     every lane that builds project-a, which is exactly the cost the cache was meant to save.
     - Log eviction events at debug level so they can be traced without flooding the default output.
